title: PredictionResidual
description: What the model said would happen, what was actually measured, and the gap between them. The loop closes here. A residual is only meaningful if the prediction existed before the measurement, so a commitment recorded before the run is required rather than optional: without it the comparison is a model fitted to a result and then congratulated for matching it.

residual.description: measured - predicted, as an Estimate. Always derived: no instrument measured a gap.

interval.description: The prediction interval the model gave, if it gave one.

within_interval.description: Whether the measurement fell inside that interval. Null when no interval was committed to, which is itself worth seeing: a point prediction with no interval cannot be wrong in a way anyone agreed on beforehand.

counts_as_model_evidence.description: Whether this residual says anything about whether the model is right. False for a synthetic stand-in, for a measurement with no replication, and for a prediction of a parameter the model does not cover.

source.description: Where the prediction came from. A human expectation is recorded the same way and is held to the same before-the-run rule.

values_sha256.description: Hash of the predicted values as committed. A prediction that is edited after the result is in is a different prediction, and this is what makes that visible.

source.description: synthetic_standin is a workflow demonstration and never biological evidence, so a residual against one never counts as model evidence.
